Subject: Compute allocation playbook — term options & GPU cost contingency

Hi Alex / Procurement team,

Great to meet last week — thanks for the detailed workload profile. Per our discussion, I’m sending two practical reserved-capacity options that balance Orion’s run-rate needs with protection against GPU-market swings. Attached are a quick SOW draft and a spreadsheet with price-sensitivity scenarios.

High-level offers:
- Option A: 12 month reserved pool (baseline 40% of observed peak) — 18% committed discount off list. Short ramp (60 days) and standard SLAs.
- Option B: 36 month reserved pool (phased activation) — 28% committed discount, lower unit price and priority burst capacity.

GPU-cost contingency (proposed constructs to address your procurement ask):
- Indexation window: quarterly review where we compare our GPU unit cost index to a baseline; if GPU spot-equivalent prices move >20%, a one-time credit or rate adjustment is triggered.
- Escrow safety: customer credit bucket that accrues if we initiate a material pass-through; offsets future invoices.
- Collar / floor: a minimum pass-through floor to avoid black-swan cost exposure for Redwood.

We can also propose a 24-month middle path with a 22% discount and a narrower contingency trigger if that helps procurement tradeoffs.

Next steps: please confirm which term you want us to model (12 / 24 / 36) and any target maximum annualized GPU price increase you want in contract language (e.g., 15% / 20% / 25%). I’ll loop in Finance & RevOps for approval flows once you signal a preferred path.

Thanks — I’ll be on standby to jump on a quick call to walk the scenarios live.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Kimberly —

Appreciate the crisp options. A few quick responses from our side after internal review:  
- We’d prefer a 24-month path if you can get 20%+ committed pricing with clear protections around GPU cost volatility.
- Procurement wants a hard cap on our annual bill increase tied to GPU market moves (they suggested a 20% cap), or alternately an escrow-credit approach that prevents surprise invoices.
- We also asked for a 90-day pilot (non-reserved) to validate tail-latency and cache-hit assumptions before the committed period starts.

Can Redwood do a 24m @ 22% with a 20% annual bill-increase cap OR a matching escrow mechanism that limits our downside? If so we’ll move to redlines.

If it helps, cc’d is our procurement lead (procurement@orion-analytics.com). Happy to set a 30-min call Thurs to finalize.

—Alex

Subject: Fwd: Orion pricing ask — approval path & suggested response

Folks — forwarding Orion’s reply (below). Procurement is asking for: 24m term, ~22% committed discount, and either a 20% annual bill-cap tied to GPU cost moves or an escrow/credit alternative. They also want a 90-day pilot preceding committed activation.

Quick take and ask:
- I think a 24m @ 22% with a conditional escrow-credit (to be applied if we pass-through >10% of baseline GPU cost) is a reasonable commercial middle ground that preserves our margin levers and product guarantees.
- We should keep a narrow collar (e.g., triggers at +/-20% from baseline GPU index) rather than a per-token pass-through at small deltas — that protects both sides from noise.
- Approvals: Finance needs to sign off on any discount >18% and any escrow mechanics. If we go >20% discount or remove the collar entirely, we’ll need Marissa for exec sign-off.

Can Finance run the sensitivity (attach if you want the spreadsheet I sent) and confirm if 22% + escrow is an acceptable max? If Finance signs off, I’ll propose the updated SOW to Orion and ask Legal to draft the trigger language.

Thanks — Kim

Kim / team —

I ran the scenarios on the attached workbook (GPU-pricing-scenarios.xlsx stub). Key points:
- Baseline: current blended GPU unit cost we expect for the next 12 months.
- If we offer 24m @ 22% with a collar trigger at +/-20%, our modeled payback still meets CFO thresholds if GPU wholesale costs drift up to ~18%. Beyond that, profits compress significantly unless we have pass-through mechanics.

Recommendation (Finance):
- Approve up to 20% non-recurring discount without exec approval. For 21-24%, require VP (Marissa) sign-off. 22% is defensible if we pair it with an escrow-credit that caps customer invoice movement and preserves Redwood’s downside protection.
- Approve a 90-day pilot (non-reserved) but require that pilot metrics & acceptance criteria are defined up-front (latency, throughput, cache hit rate). Pilot must convert within 90 days of acceptance or revert to list pricing.
- Suggest a simple clause: quarterly GPU-index review; if our GPU cost delta >25% vs baseline, we reserve the right to trigger a negotiated pass-through with a 60-day notice and an escrow offset equal to X% of the delta. Legal can draft precise language.

Happy to present the numbers if helpful.

-Aditya Rao
Senior Manager, Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference
